- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., recent sentiment change > 0.33) and model forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative sharply (e.g., sentiment change < -0.33) and forecast is high, apply downward correction to prevent overshoot.  
- Model tends to overestimate prices during sentiment spikes; apply a 5–10% downward bias after a sentiment peak.  
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 3–5% to align with mean reversion.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; use sentiment smoothing to dampen noise.  
- If news volume is low (e.g., 0.0) and sentiment is stable, model may overfit recent trends; apply a 2–5% downward adjustment to avoid false momentum.  
- Model consistently overestimates in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon; apply a 3–7% downward correction for early periods.  
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 2–5% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
